item.text:
**Bottom line:** Mixed, but slightly positive on macroeconomic professionalism. The clearest 2024 evidence shows AMLO keeping a respected finance technocrat in place and publicly defending stable rules, while the negative case is mostly indirect: broader power-concentration and rule-of-law warnings, not a smoking gun of economic patronage.

- **Economía de México es sólida y hay responsabilidad en manejo de finanzas: presidente** — Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 / Gobierno de México, 2024-06-04. [URL](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/economia-de-mexico-es-solida-y-hay-responsabilidad-en-manejo-de-finanzas-presidente/). AMLO said financial management was responsible, the economy was solid, and the policy would not change because keeping the existing rules preserved economic and financial stability. This supports technocratic macro continuity more than loyalty politics. IDs: `5B.2`, `5B.1`.

- **Mexican finance minister seeks to soothe investors, reduce public debt** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-06-04. [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/mexican-finance-minister-seeks-to-soothe-investors-reduce-public-debt-3470241). Rogelio Ramírez de la O stayed on, promised lower debt and fiscal discipline, said the government would refresh communication with investors and rating agencies, and explicitly backed central bank autonomy and the rule of law. Strong positive evidence for competent economic professionals being empowered. IDs: `5B.2`, `5B.1`.

- **Readout: Secretary of the Treasury Janet L. Yellen’s Call with Finance Secretary Rogelio Ramírez de la O of Mexico** — U.S. Department of the Treasury, 2024-06-21. [URL](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2423). Treasury treated Ramírez de la O as the continuity point for Mexico’s economic policy after his reappointment and discussed investment screening and payment-system connectivity with him. That is consistent with a technocratic, credible economic team. ID: `5B.2`.

- **Versión estenográfica. Conferencia de prensa del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador del 5 de septiembre de 2024** — Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 / Gobierno de México, 2024-09-05. [URL](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/articulos/version-estenografica-conferencia-de-prensa-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-del-5-de-septiembre-de-2024). AMLO said banks had record profits and that not changing banking rules was the price of maintaining stability. That cuts against short-term populist meddling and suggests he was willing to leave macro rules in technocratic hands. IDs: `5B.2`, `5B.1`.

- **Analysis-Mexico investors worry lopsided vote could threaten rule of law** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-06-07. [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/analysismexico-investors-worry-lopsided-vote-could-threaten-rule-of-law-3475796). Reuters reported investor concern that AMLO might use the post-election mandate to sweep aside checks on presidential power during his final month. This is indirect but meaningful negative evidence that political control could outrank technocratic restraint. IDs: `5B.2`, `4B.10`.

- **Mexico proposed constitutional changes threaten rights** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-08-30. [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights). HRW warned the reform package could weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy and transparency safeguards. That is negative indirect evidence against a clean technocratic-empowerment story. IDs: `5B.2`, `4B.10`.

- **World Report 2024: Mexico** — Human Rights Watch, 2024. [URL](https://www.hrw.org/es/world-report/2024/country-chapters/mexico). HRW said AMLO and his party blocked appointments to INAI, leaving the transparency/data-protection body unable to function normally. This is not an economic appointment, but it supports the broader pattern that independent professional bodies were not always empowered. IDs: `5B.2`, `4B.10`.

**Search gap:** I found direct 2024 evidence of technocratic continuity at Hacienda and public support for stable macro rules, but little direct 2024 evidence of AMLO making new economic appointments that were clearly loyalist, familial, or business-linked. The strongest negatives are broader institutional-centralization signals, not explicit economic staffing abuses.
